FNIS 100.title: Indigenous Foundations
FNIS 100.description: The historical, cultural, political, economic and legal issues that inform the experiences of Indigenous peoples in Canada, examined from both Indigenous and non-Indigenous perspectives. Restricted to Undergraduate Students.

FNIS 210.title: Indigenous Politics and Self-Determination
FNIS 210.description: The cultural, historical, political, economic, and gender dynamics that structure the relationship between Indigenous peoples and the state in Canada; Indigenous self-determination struggles in relation to constitutional recognition, self-government, land claims, and economic development. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Recommended pre-requisite: FNIS 100.

FNIS 220.title: Representation and Indigenous Cultural Politics
FNIS 220.description: Representation, identity, and cultural politics through Indigenous literature, film, and the visual arts; the relationship between these sites of cultural production and the self-determination struggles of Indigenous peoples. Restricted to Undergraduate Students. Recommended pre-requisite: FNIS 100

FNIS 260.title: Applied Learning: Collaborative Place-Based Research
FNIS 260.description: Topic and community/location of instruction will vary from year to year. Applied, intense delivery experiential learning course designed and implemented in collaboration with faculty and Indigenous community partner(s). Examines the importance of Indigenous place-based research and learning for student and community empowerment. Restricted to Undergraduate Students.

FNIS 300.title: Writing First Nations
FNIS 300.description: writing-intensive course examining approaches to writing Indigenous research: Representation & the Other; Indigenous critiques of research & representation; Indigenous, feminist and cultural studies approaches to writing ethnography, oral history, and related research methods. Restricted to Undergraduate Students.
FNIS 300.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of FNIS_V 210, FNIS_V 220 or (b) one of FNSP_V 210, FNSP_V 220

FNIS 310.title: Critical Indigenous Theory Seminar
FNIS 310.description: Adapting and integrating current conceptual paradigms in the humanities, social sciences, performing arts, and Indigenous studies into approaches in First Nations/Indigenous Studies, including identity construction, political and cultural self-determination, representation, essentialism/authenticity, ethics, and decolonization. Restricted to Undergraduate Students.
FNIS 310.prerequisiteText: Either (a) FNSP_V 200 or (b) all of FNIS_V 210, FNIS_V 220 or (c) all of FNSP_V 210, FNSP_V 220

FNIS 320.title: Critical Indigenous Methodologies and Ethics
FNIS 320.description: Responsible and community-based research from a critical Indigenous perspective; methods for identifying and assessing research materials, critical analysis, oral history/qualitative research interviewing and analysis, and research ethics in the design and implementation of community-based student research projects. Restricted to Undergraduate Students.

FNIS 360.title: Applied Learning: Collaborative Place-Based Research
FNIS 360.description: Topic and community/location of instruction will vary from year to year. Applied, intense delivery experiential learning course designed and implemented in collaboration with faculty and Indigenous community partner(s). Examines the importance of Indigenous place-based research and learning for student and community empowerment. Restricted to Undergraduate Students.
FNIS 360.prerequisiteText: One of FNSP_V 200, FNIS_V 210, FNSP_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 220. And Permission of the Instructor

FNIS 400.title: Practicum/Advanced Research Seminar
FNIS 400.description: Applied research/community oriented project designed and implemented in collaboration with student, faculty and Aboriginal community organization. Emphasis on examining ethical issues and developing culturally respectful and academically rigorous forms of research. Restricted to Majors in First Nations and Indigenous Studies.

FNIS 400.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of FNIS_V 310, FNIS_V 320 or (b) all of FNSP_V 310, FNSP_V 320. Students must pass FNIS_V 320 or FNSP_V 320 with a B- or higher or request program approval

FNIS 401.title: Special Topics
FNIS 401.description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consult the departmental website: Restricted to Undergraduate Students.
FNIS 401.prerequisiteText: One of FNIS 100, FNSP 200, FNIS 210, FNSP 210, FNIS 220, FNSP 220

FNIS 451.title: Indigenous Feminisms
FNIS 451.description: The historical, cultural, political, and activist roots of contemporary Indigenous feminisms. Indigenous feminist methodologies, theory, and praxis in relation to contemporary Indigenous politics and social justice movements. Restricted to Undergraduate Students.
FNIS 451.prerequisiteText: One of FNIS_V 100, FNSP_V 200, FNIS_V 210, FNSP_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 220

FNIS 452.title: Indigenous Social Movements
FNIS 452.description: Draws on Indigenous and non-Indigenous intellectual traditions to explore the theoretical, cultural, political, economic, and historical bases of Indigenous peoples decolonization struggles in Canada. Restricted to Undergraduate Students.
FNIS 452.prerequisiteText: One of FNIS_V 100, FNSP_V 200, FNIS_V 210, FNSP_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 220

FNIS 453.title: Indigenous Legal Traditions
FNIS 453.description: Socio-historical, political and cultural context of Indigenous legal traditions and strategies for ethical engagement within state and Indigenous polities. Methods include oral history analysis, legal theory, literary/narrative studies, and philosophy from an Indigenous studies perspective. Restricted to Undergraduate Students.
FNIS 453.prerequisiteText: One of FNIS_V 100, FNSP_V 200, FNIS_V 210, FNSP_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 220

FNIS 454.title: Indigenous New Media
FNIS 454.description: New media and digital storytelling works designed and implemented by Indigenous artists, authors, and programmers. Restricted to Undergraduate Students.
FNIS 454.prerequisiteText: One of FNIS_V 100, FNSP_V 200, FNIS_V 210, FNSP_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 220

FNIS 455.title: Indigenous Geographies: Our Home on Native Land
FNIS 455.description: Indigenous people's place-based relations, colonial processes of de-territorialization, and spatial negotiations of settler colonialism. Restricted to Undergraduate Students.
FNIS 455.prerequisiteText: One of FNIS_V 100, FNSP_V 200, FNIS_V 210, FNSP_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 220

FNIS 456.title: Indigenous Two-Spirit and Queer Studies
FNIS 456.description: Cultural contexts, scholarship, literature, and artistic expressions of Queer, LGBTI, and Two-Spirited Indigenous people, both as an academic area of study and as lived experience and relationship. Restricted to Undergraduate Students.
FNIS 456.prerequisiteText: One of FNIS_V 100, FNIS_V 210, FNIS_V 220, FNSP_V 200, FNSP_V 210, FNSP_V 220

FNIS 560.title: Applied Learning: Collaborative Place-Based Research
FNIS 560.description: Applied, immersive experiential learning course designed and implemented in collaboration with faculty and Indigenous community partner(s). Emphasis on examining the importance of Indigenous place-based research and learning for student and community empowerment. Topic and community/location of instruction will vary from year to year.
